title: Local Folders
blurb: Local Folders appears below connected accounts and stays available after those accounts are disconnected. The plus (New local folder) and Import MBOX icon buttons beside its heading show tooltips and support keyboard focus. New local folder creates a folder; right-click a folder, or focus it and press Shift + F10, to create a subfolder, rename it or delete it when empty. Archive and Trash are permanent. The message menu starts with Move to folder… and Move / Copy to other mailbox…, followed by Labels…, Mark as read/unread, Star/Unstar, Move to trash and Archive where supported. Right-click targets the clicked message unless it belongs to the current multi-selection; actions keep the reviewed message IDs and mailbox connection without expanding conversations. A reconnect retires the old review even before the account list refreshes. Unsubmitted reviewed menu actions expire on restart. Shift + F10 or the Menu key opens the row menu; arrows and Home/End navigate, and Escape closes it and restores focus. Gmail Labels keeps its existing permission; IMAP, Yahoo, Outlook and Local Folders use folder actions. Move to trash never permanently deletes; already-Trash sources are blocked and rechecked by the host. The combined transfer dialog chooses Copy or Move and a Local Folders destination for up to 200 saved messages, including hidden selections. Connected receiving mailboxes offer capability-checked Copy; see Cross-mailbox Copy for provider requirements, review and recovery limits. The reader also has Local Folders. Copy downloads the complete original MIME message, all headers, text/HTML, recipients, dates and inline/file attachments; partial cached bodies and temporary attachment downloads are not archives. Move verifies the saved copy before moving the server original to recoverable provider Trash. Gmail Trash affects the message across all labels; provider retention may later empty Trash. IMAP Move requires server MOVE support; other IMAP servers can Copy. A connection and free space are needed for a first server copy, with a 64 MiB original-message limit; Gmail retains its existing 35 MiB API limit. Transfers run one message at a time. Stop after this message or Escape stops remaining messages after the current one finishes and cannot recall a started server move. Failed or uncertain remote moves retain the local copy and show the result; check the server before retrying an uncertain move. Restart never replays server Trash. Repeated transfers to the same destination reuse their verified local copy even if it was later moved locally. Gmail label copies with a known canonical provider identity share the same transfer receipt. Offline reading, attachment preview/Open/Save/ZIP, read/star flags, local copy/move, local Trash/restore and original EML export work without account authentication. Remote images keep the existing image policy and require a network connection. Entering Local Folders defaults search to its local archive. Local phrase search uses the same Unicode normalization and lowercasing for archived subject, sender, To and plain text and for the query; accents remain significant. An explicit All connected accounts or connected-account search scope stays selected across queries and account refreshes; entering a local folder starts a new local scope. All connected accounts and All Account Mail exclude local copies. Filter downloaded view matches all saved messages in the selected local folder before paging. The reader Trash button follows the selected local messages, including rows hidden by this filter; independent readers keep their own single-message scope. Local Trash has no permanent-delete or automatic-empty action; move a message to another local folder to restore it. Nonempty folders cannot be deleted. Local Folders cannot send, reply, resume drafts, run AI mail actions, sync, receive bot/CLI operations or drag folders/messages. Use the reviewed Cross-mailbox Copy action to copy eligible local messages to a supported connected mailbox. Use Import MBOX for supported mailbox exports. New mail still uses a connected sending account. Local mail stays in this computer's app profile; back up local-folders.sqlite with Morrow closed. Removing an account never removes it. Native Windows/macOS provider behavior and power-loss recovery are not certified by synthetic tests.
